hook: Airbags, gym mats and the crumple zones in cars do not change how much a body must slow down in a crash. They change how long the slowing takes. Impulse explains why stretching out the time is all it takes to turn a bone-breaking force into a survivable one.

ideas: Impulse J = F_avg Δt, a vector along the force, in N·s (= kg·m/s). It is the area under a force-time graph.
The impulse-momentum theorem: J_net = Δp = m v_f − m v_i. Keep the signs: a bounce reverses v.
The same Δp over a longer time needs a smaller force: airbags, mats, bent knees.
F_net = Δp/Δt, the slope of a momentum-time graph. For constant mass this is Newton's second law, F_net = ma.

misconception.wrong: Momentum is force times time, so p = Ft.
misconception.right: Force times time is the impulse, which equals the change in momentum, Δp = F_avg Δt. Momentum itself is mv.

summary: Impulse J = F_avg Δt is the area under a force-time graph, and it equals the change in momentum. A fixed change in momentum spread over more time needs less force. The slope of a momentum-time graph is the net force.
